title: Software and data maintenance
description: Keep Windows healthy with updates, storage clean-up, the right drive optimisation, malware scans and a backup plan.
objectives: Keep Windows, drivers and applications updated.
Know why hard drives are defragmented but SSDs are not.
tools: External drive or cloud storage for backups

safety.text: Check what you are deleting. Never delete files from Windows system folders by hand.
Do not interrupt the computer while updates install: it can leave Windows unable to start.

steps.title: Update everything
steps.body:
- **Windows Update:** Settings → Windows Update → Check for updates. Install security updates promptly.
- **Drivers:** most come through Windows Update. Graphics and chipset drivers can be newer on the maker's website.
- **Applications:** update browsers and other software, or remove programs that are no longer used.

steps.title: Free up storage
steps.body:
Windows needs free space to update and run well; keep at least **15–20%** free.

- **Settings → System → Storage** shows what is using space and **Cleanup recommendations**.
- Turn on **Storage Sense** to delete temporary files automatically.
- Uninstall unused programs in **Settings → Apps**.

steps.title: Optimise the drives correctly
steps.body:
Open **Defragment and Optimize Drives**:

- **Hard disk drives (HDD):** defragmenting puts the pieces of files back together, which speeds them up.
- **SSDs:** do **not** defragment. Windows sends **TRIM** instead, which keeps the SSD fast. Defragmenting an SSD only adds wear.

Leave the scheduled optimisation on: Windows chooses the right method for each drive.

steps.title: Scan for malware
steps.body: **Windows Security** (Microsoft Defender) protects in real time. Run a **Quick scan** regularly and a **Full scan** if you suspect infection. Only use one real-time antivirus at a time; two conflict.

steps.title: Check drive health
steps.body: Drives warn before they fail through **S.M.A.R.T.** data. A disk health tool (such as CrystalDiskInfo) reads it. Reallocated or pending sectors on an HDD, or low remaining life on an SSD, mean: back up and plan a replacement.

steps.title: Back up with the 3-2-1 rule
steps.body:
- **3** copies of important data,
- on **2** different types of storage (for example the PC and an external drive),
- with **1** copy off-site (cloud, or a drive kept elsewhere).

Test restoring a file now and then: a backup you cannot restore is not a backup.

expectedResults: Windows and drivers are up to date.
At least 15–20% of the system drive is free.
The customer has a working 3-2-1 backup.

commonMistakes.why: It does not speed up an SSD and adds unnecessary wear.
commonMistakes.fix: Let Windows optimise it with TRIM.

commonMistakes.why: They conflict, slow the computer and can block each other.
commonMistakes.fix: Use one: Microsoft Defender is built in.

commonMistakes.mistake: Keeping the only backup on the same computer.
commonMistakes.why: A drive failure, theft or ransomware takes the backup too.
commonMistakes.fix: Follow 3-2-1 with an external and an off-site copy.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why shouldn't you defragment an SSD?
knowledgeChecks.answer: It gives no speed benefit and adds wear. Windows keeps SSDs fast with TRIM.

knowledgeChecks.question: What does 3-2-1 mean?
knowledgeChecks.answer: 3 copies, on 2 types of storage, 1 kept off-site.
